t: You're looking at a bronze memorial plaque to the architect Richard Norman Shaw, set on the Norman Shaw Buildings. Shaw worked from the eighteen seventies to the nineteen hundreds, known for country houses and commercial buildings, and he's considered among the greatest of British architects. His influence was strongest in the eighteen eighties and nineties. The plaque was made by Hamo Thornycroft, the sculptor behind London's statue of Oliver Cromwell outside the Palace of Westminster. So one celebrated Londoner is remembered here by another.
